reviews.text: I got bored. Felt very bland & milquetoast. The female portraits are attractive, but the female soldiers are in sexless robo-suits. You get to shoot things, but there is no blood or gibs. It all feels a bit too tame & family friendly. I kept wanting to use number keys to switch weapons, but the number keys are bound to abilities, & there is no way to bind keys to specific weapon slots. You don't notice when you are low on health because there is no heartbeat sound or red vignette to let you know you are near death, so you drop dead for what feels like no reason with all your health items unused.

It's got huge battlefields to fight on, it's got roguelike builds that change every run, it's got base-building and enemy capturing, it's got NPC management, farming, crafting, it's got tanks, mechs, elites, and bosses with crazy abilities… Honestly, it's got everything a player could ask for.

饼画的很大，各种玩法都融了一些，武器装备、职业、科技树、功能建筑庞杂但都不够深而且没什么联动。其次核心玩法的肉鸽池就现在看到的太浅了，战斗手感又一般，只能说欠缺打磨。应先重点着眼于战斗和肉鸽上，好好优化一下。 然后在家园内的无限制飞行和盖房子自动给浮空+网格辅助我觉得思路正确，基底建设底子也做的有模有样，深一点的模拟和建筑布局都可以因为才demo跳过不说，但你这局外养成除了磨时间建出来对应工坊造了一身基础装备外和局内战斗有什么关系吗？ 而士兵外派和捉宠说白了就是很鸡肋，先不说肉鸽能不能选到对应增益，你都有家园养成和身心状态部分了，士兵外派肯定会想着做受伤或者疲劳什么的，那你这局内看着就很一般还占了肉鸽池又占了建筑资源甚至时间资源的带队出征有什么好拿出手的吗？ 鸡肋且割裂成这样，只能说三边不讨好。 一开始是对游戏的花式标签有点兴趣，但玩了会儿感觉游戏需要改动甚至删减的东西太多了点，要是EA版就这么端上来那真一般，而且按这个制作来说真铺开做了肯定要浪费大量人力物力，定价肯定不会低，现在兴趣更多的是在于想看看你们游戏后续是怎么个定位和改法。

I saw this on Splattercat's channel and watched his vid before coming to check this out myself. It seemed interesting and certainly had a different flavor to other colony games I have played which promised a fresh experience. However, I wasn't very impressed overall. I'm giving it a thumbs down for visibility but it would be neutral if Steam allowed such. (Also, I wanted to say real quick at the start that counter to Gammonzilla's negative review decrying the sexless armor female humans wear, as a woman myself I am grateful for any depiction of women that is not inherently sexualized. It makes sense that women in power armor or bulky environment suits would not look drastically different to men, thank you for not putting them in boob plate or something.) The game is very pretty in the 1st person sections, even on my archaic system, but overall the game is kind of just middling in my opinion. It incorporates systems from a wide variety of genres, but no one aspect of it was particularly engaging which may be due to being too broad in scope? I'm not saying the devs should cut out any of what is present, just that what is present feels like it needs more work to start feeling good. [list] [*] Resource gathering is terrible as the player but you have to engage in it early on. Holding the F key for several minutes to get the resources that you need to do the next task in getting started is so damn annoying. There were plenty of times during the first 30-45 minutes that I was on the verge of just quitting the game. Not because I was having to gather, but because gathering is slow [b]and[/b] you have to [u]hold a specific key[/u] to do it. On the other hand, later on once you have all the resources covered by bots resources are essentially negligible, so it feels like there is no middle ground. I also dislike that the player gathers so much slower than bots. I get that this is may be to help steer the player into the mindset that laborers should be doing the labor, but there doesn't seem to be a way to speed up the day (and thus progress on work) which leaves the player either going AFK or participating in an annoying system. [*] Base building is basic, but I like the build-mode for a 1st person game, and also that buildings can be moved for free, great choice. I would say that it is cool that the player can participate in the act of construction, but as with resource gathering, the player's contribution is significantly lower than that of bots so it feels pointless outside of very specific instances. [*] Combat felt... clunky? I'm not sure. I enjoy shooters in either 3rd or 1st person perspective, but I was really struggling to hit anything in this game's combat. I ended up just using the shotgun at point-blank range almost exclusively. It might help if there was a cover/peeking mechanic, especially if the bots would use it. Also, the reticule needs contrast from the background. I was having trouble seeing it in too many instances. Give it a black border or something at the bare minimum. [*] You can take bots with you when you go fight but they are dumb as rocks and fall easily (at least early on, where the starter bot seems to die with only a couple kills and little damage dealt compared to damage taken seeming to indicate it is only getting kills because it is finishing off something I was attacking), and only the starter bot won't die permanently so I avoid taking bots into combat which makes combat a slog. The only fun combat missions I came across were ones where several allied soldiers spawned in and you were all attacking en masse thus spreading out the incoming damage and just being more visually interesting. [*] Stellar exploration is serviceable, but feels like it could be cut entirely and little would be lost. Like, encounter generation could be a function of interacting with the shuttle or a scanner placed in the base and it would result in essentially the same gameplay. To be clear I don't want it cut, but I feel like it needs something to jazz it up. I like that POI detection is done in a limited radius, and I imagine that different ships later on will alter that radius, but it would be nice if there was some indication of where you had explored already as either fog of war or maybe a visible trail of where the ship has flown. I think something that I dislike is that click+drag is not a viable control and instead you navigate only by clicking. This makes me feel detached from what is going on. I would much rather fly the ship in a 3d space, but I recognize that is likely well beyond the scope of the game and also pointless without some sort of in-space dogfight encounters, so adding in click+drag would allow for a sense of direct control without needing to build a 3d space flight section. [/list] The whole theme of the game is that you're a loyal, brain-washed commander serving an authoritarian regime looking for an opportunity to invade a neighboring power. You're supposed to be this uncaring overlord managing an army of disposable fodder, but because you struggle early on to even have workers you end up treating them like a precious commodity and don't use them in all roles for fear of losing them and setting yourself back horrendously. Maybe this is an issue with me approaching the game incorrectly, but it seems to defeat the purpose. I dunno, maybe getting new laborers is super easy, barely an inconvenience even, but that hasn't been apparent to me so far and only nearly three hours in do I now have laborers I don't specifically need. Also, the tutorial... So often is it the case that the player is cast as some esteemed leader of men, a tactical prodigy, a brilliant strategist playing 4-d chess; but the tutorial is written to where some underling is talking to you like you're a know-nothing idiot. This game is no different. I long for a game written to where the tutorial is the experienced player character directing fresh-faced recruits in the intricacies of whatever the game is about, and over the course of the experience they are forged into a capable force. Maybe these last two complaints of mine are supposed to be part of the satire? If so, it felt like they missed the mark for me. In closing, I have wishlisted the main game to keep tabs on it and would be likely to purchase it so long as it isn't priced like a triple-A title, so my negative review shouldn't be seen as condemnation or whatever. I think this could be a good game and I am interested to see how it turns out.

Pax Autocratica has a lot of potential, but was a very jarring experience for me. The core on-foot gameplay is good, with impactful gunplay and incredibly fast and fairly smooth movement. The base building has a wealth of options when it comes to various production and gameplay-effecting buildings, but there's no way to alter terrain and limited options for connecting sctructures, my base ended up looking like a bit of an awkward collage. This game seems to me aiming very high, and I think that its goals are very possibly achievable, but it currently comes with what I find a major cost: lack of clear direction and identity. The way the game is presented on Steam and in the trailer shows a very clear identity, but when actually playing there's a very strange mash of art styles, ideas, mechanics, and tone that ends up making the game feel like a showcase of purchased/obtained assets and placeholders. The foundation is here, but I think it needs a better sense of direction and identity with a fair amount of glue to tie in all the various concepts and ideas before I'd consider it to be a presentable product. If there was a neutral review score option I would've picked that, but given the choices I'm leaning more towards negative than positive. With that said, I look forward to the games future and would happily purchase and give the full game a positive review if things change.

This game checks a lot of boxes. Its fairly smooth for early access (demo). You have the FPS portion that feels smooth, aiming is good. Movement is fast. You also have the base building. You can research a variety of buildings. You or your soldier minions can harvest resources on your base map as well as gather them during FPS expeditions. You can recruit soldiers for your cause. You can set them up to work for you around your base as well as choose some to go with you in FPS mode. You can also capture enemies and bend them to your will, or just execute them. You can even imprison your own soldiers to teach them a lesson or simply keep them all in line. Only 2 hours in and I'm addicted. If you like base building, fps, or resource management give the demo a go. I look forward to expanded content. An will be putting it at the top of my wishlist.

优点：超级缝合怪，好喜欢！ 上帝视角，搞基建、拉经济、颁布政令统治整个星球；一边切第一人称亲自上战场，从巷战步兵到开重型坦克、驾巨型机甲，两种玩法切换完全不割裂。前一秒还在纠结要不要加税，下一秒就端着枪冲去平叛，爽感和策略感直接拉满。 “立法权” 系统真的有深度 这不是随便点几个选项的摆设：你可以装全境监控搞高压统治，也可以建医院学校走仁政路线。每一条政令都会真实影响殖民地的一切 —— 民众的幸福度、犯罪率、叛乱概率，甚至连工人的生产效率都会跟着变。玩的时候真的会有 “手握权力” 的沉重感，社会隐喻做得很到位。 Roguelike 战斗超出预期 每次出征都是随机增益，没有完全一样的两场战斗。武器种类很丰富，从突击步枪到反坦克炮都有，打击感扎实，大规模集团作战的场面也很震撼。试玩版就能体验到机甲对战，正式版的内容量值得期待。 缺点：还有不少打磨空间 新手引导严重不足，殖民模拟的很多核心机制都没讲清楚，刚上手很容易一头雾水，不知道该先建什么、怎么平衡民生和军事。 优化有待提升，大规模战斗或者殖民地人口多了之后，会出现明显的掉帧和卡顿。 试玩版内容还是有限，立法选项和武器种类都不多，后期会有点重复。 UI 交互比较繁琐，切换视角和操作菜单的时候不够流畅。 总结 这绝对是 2026 年开年最值得期待的独立游戏之一。虽然被很多人叫 “缝合怪”，但它把完全不同的玩法融合得非常好，而且有自己独特的世界观和深度。

Pax Autocratica: Prologue, developed and published by Multiverse, is a fascinating experiment that blends genres rarely seen together. At its core, it is a colony management game set in a grim science-fiction future, but it layers that foundation with roguelite progression and first-person shooter mechanics. Players assume the role of an all-powerful leader tasked with establishing order across a hostile world, making decisions that determine whether their society thrives through benevolence or survives through fear. The game's premise immediately stands out because it does not shy away from exploring themes of authoritarianism, social engineering, and the price of maintaining absolute control. The management systems provide the backbone of the experience. Players oversee a growing settlement where citizens gather resources, construct facilities, conduct research, and contribute to the expansion of the State. Unlike many strategy games where inhabitants feel interchangeable, Pax Autocratica attempts to give its population a sense of individuality. Policies enacted by the player can inspire devotion or resentment, and maintaining stability becomes an ongoing challenge. Decisions involving propaganda, surveillance, punishment, and ideological influence are central to progression, giving the game a distinctly dystopian flavor that sets it apart from more traditional city builders. One of the title's most ambitious features is its shift from overhead management to direct participation in combat. Rather than simply dispatching units to battle and watching the results, players enter the field themselves in first-person engagements. These missions are fast-paced and heavily inspired by roguelite design, with enemy waves featuring soldiers, machines, and powerful bosses. Combat encounters are filled with projectiles, explosive attacks, and environmental hazards that require constant movement and quick decision-making. The transition between managing a colony and leading troops in battle creates a unique gameplay loop that feels fresh, even if it occasionally struggles to balance both sides of its identity. Progression is another area where the prologue shows considerable promise. Players can unlock upgrades that alter weapons, improve combat capabilities, and create synergistic combinations between abilities. Every expedition offers opportunities to experiment with different builds, ensuring that repeated runs feel distinct. Supporting units can also be enhanced, turning them into valuable companions during combat or expendable assets depending on the player's preferred approach. Although the available content is intentionally limited, the systems on display suggest a much larger and more complex experience planned for the full release. The game's darker mechanics contribute significantly to its atmosphere. Defeated enemies can be captured and returned to the colony, where players decide their fate. They may be imprisoned, indoctrinated into the regime, or permanently removed as threats. These choices reinforce the overarching themes of power and control while encouraging players to think beyond simple battlefield victories. Pax Autocratica consistently challenges players to consider the ethical consequences of their actions, even if its presentation occasionally leans into dark humor and satire. As expected from a prologue, there are limitations that prevent the experience from reaching its full potential. Content is restricted to a small portion of the planned campaign, and some mechanics feel unfinished or in need of additional refinement. Balance issues occasionally emerge during combat, and certain systems could benefit from clearer explanations. Nevertheless, the game succeeds in demonstrating the developers' vision. It serves less as a complete product and more as a compelling invitation to what Multiverse hopes to achieve with the eventual full release. Visually, the game captures its oppressive science-fiction setting effectively. Industrial landscapes, militarized architecture, and chaotic battle sequences help establish a memorable atmosphere. The audio design complements the experience with fitting effects and music that maintain tension throughout both colony management and combat scenarios. While it does not possess the production values of larger studios, its artistic direction compensates by delivering a cohesive and distinctive identity. Pax Autocratica: Prologue is an ambitious hybrid that refuses to remain within the boundaries of a single genre. Its combination of strategy, action, and roguelite elements makes it one of the more intriguing indie projects currently available on Steam. Though rough around the edges and limited by its status as a prologue, it offers enough depth and originality to leave a lasting impression. Players willing to embrace its unusual mechanics and morally complex themes will find an experience that feels both experimental and promising. Rating: 7/10
